dependency_anchors.text:
Six job routes resolve configured providers, accounts, model profiles and model/depth pairs.
Easy, routine jobs inherits Everyday building when blank and handles only small, low-risk, non-GUI implementation.
Legacy lane bindings are compatibility reads; ambiguous retired maps are disclosed and do not write new job defaults automatically.
A required job with no usable model after inheritance blocks with recovery instead of choosing arbitrarily.
Cheap implementation never acts as verifier, adjudicator or certifier; checking and implementation remain distinct requests.
Parent-selected helper model and effort obey actual authority, availability and policy ceilings without a separate Settings row.
Receipts preserve requested/effective identity and capability evidence.
Model routing uses six jobs: Planning and supervising (overseer), Everyday building (worker), Easy, routine jobs (low_effort_worker), Design and layout (gui_frontend_worker), The hardest jobs (high_effort_worker), and Checking finished work (auditor). Resolve the configured model/depth through §2; a blank job follows Everyday model, except Easy, routine jobs follows Everyday building. Keep configured provider/account/model-profile identity, capability evidence and requested/effective receipts. Old low_cost_executor maps to low_effort_worker, standard_reviewer/verifier/adjudicator/certifier map to auditor, high_reasoning_orchestrator maps to overseer as compatibility input names only, without restoring retired Goal roles. Missing usable models after named inheritance return typed blocked states with recovery; never arbitrary defaults. Preserve per-piece build policies, parent ceilings and separate checking versus implementation selections. Helpers may use any parent-selected available model and effort; available means allowed and runnable under policy/parent ceilings, otherwise ordinary job/everyday defaults apply. Models owns no write_mode, lease or certification semantics.
